messages:
Mira Chen: Quick follow-up after the pinning RFC — can we trim what the client surface actually needs? TL;DR: prefer a compact client-visible hint set and keep the heavier rollout metadata in the control plane. Thoughts? :thinking:
Alex Novak: +1. Current pin payload is way too chatty. Clients only need a few stable fields to decide routing/fallback: model_id, variant, anchor_ts, fallback_order. Everything else (provenance, telemetry tokens, variant affinity weights) should live server-side.
Samir Patel: I agree with trimming, but we still need some provenance for debugging and audits. How do we give SREs/devs access without blowing up every client response?
Jin Park: Option: split into two surfaces — a small `client_hint` included in responses and a `server_meta` accessible from the control plane API / logs. Make `client_hint` strictly bounded in size. Also add an opt-in verbose debug endpoint for deep inspection.
Priya Rao: Operational note: Private/Dedicated customers occasionally run without control-plane connectivity. They need enough metadata to make safe fallbacks locally. So the client_hint must cover that offline-safety use case. Propose two namespaces: `client_hint` (small) and `offline_guardrails` (lightweight but durable).
Alex Novak: Good call. Suggest minimal client_hint schema example:
```
{
  "model_id": "rw/llama-3a",
  "variant": "quant-v1",
  "anchor_ts": 1690000000,
  "fallback": ["rw/llama-3b", "rw/opt-7b"],
  "rollout_id": "r-2026-03-canary"
}
```
Keep it <= ~300 bytes ideally. Everything larger (affinity weights, telemetry keys, soft-hints) stays in server_meta.
Samir Patel: We should also add an explicit `schema_version` header so clients can evolve. e.g., `X-RW-Pin-Schema: v1` — clients ignore unrecognized fields.
Mira Chen: +1 on the header. Also: migration plan?
Priya Rao: Proposed migration steps:
1) Add `client_hint` and `server_meta` fields in responses behind a feature flag.
2) Update Dedicated/Private agent to request `offline_guardrails` when control-plane unreachable.
3) Flip default to new compact hint once SDKs adopt `X-RW-Pin-Schema` handling.
4) Deprecate legacy fields after one quarter with telemetry checks.
This keeps customer safety and gives ops time to adapt.
Alex Novak: I'll draft a short RFC update and include test ideas for client fallback semantics. Will also include a compat matrix for SDK versions.
Samir Patel: One more edge: canary tokens — we currently embed rollout token blobs that are big. Instead: recommend ephemeral header `X-RW-Canary: r-2026-03-canary` and resolve server-side when possible.
Jin Park: Agree. Ephemeral small headers + control-plane detail works well.
release-bot: deploy pinned-schema-reducer -> staging :rocket:
Mira Chen: Thanks — @Alex can you take the RFC patch? If you post by EOD we can review tomorrow. Also add a short note for Private customers about the offline_guardrails expectation. :thumbsup:
Alex Novak: Yep, will post draft by EOD. Adding the Private note and `X-RW-Pin-Schema` tests.
Priya Rao: I'll coordinate with support to message affected customers during rollout.
Samir Patel: Quick follow: add a small telemetry flag to count older clients that ignore the header so we know when to deprecate fields.
Mira Chen: Perfect. I'll file a follow-up ticket to track telemetry and deprecation. Closing for now unless something urgent pops up. Thanks all. :wave:
